clauses.reason: Blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Haiti, its agencies and controlled entities, including the Banque de la Republique d'Haiti. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Lead of Sec. 2: introduces the payment, import and export prohibitions in items (a) to (d). Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits payments or transfers to the de facto regime in Haiti and directs that amounts owed to the Government of Haiti be paid into a Federal Reserve Bank of New York account for the Haitian people. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits importation into the United States of goods of Haitian origin, and of services performed in Haiti, subject to item (d). Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Prohibits exportation from the United States to Haiti of goods, technology and services other than publications, humanitarian donations, and rice, beans, sugar, wheat flour and cooking oil. Later event: EO 12853 (signed 1993-06-30) Sec. 7 revokes sections 2(c) and 4 of EO 12779 to the extent inconsistent with EO 12853, effective immediately under its Sec. 8(a); EO 12853 Sec. 3 adds prohibitions on petroleum and arms and Sec. 4 limits the food exemption in section 2(c)(iii) for transactions involving the regime or identified persons, so the revocation reaches only that overlap. Later event: EO 12917 (signed 1994-05-21) Sec. 4 revokes section 2(c) of EO 12779 to the extent inconsistent with EO 12917, effective at 11:59 p.m. EDT May 21, 1994 and applying only to actions after that time; EO 12917 Sec. 1(d) re-sets the export prohibition in its own terms, so the revocation is partial and conditional. The clause continues, as narrowed, until EO 12932. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Allows goods with parts exported from the United States before the effective date to be imported after assembly or processing in Haiti for a period of 30 days from the effective date. Sec. 6 makes the order effective as of 11:59 p.m. Eastern standard time on November 5, 1991 unless otherwise specified, so thirty days from that moment run to December 5, 1991; the end is recorded as 1991-12-05 (a computed date; counting convention is the producer's, and an exclusive count could place the end a day earlier or later). This is an own-terms period and ends well before EO 12932.

Lead of the definitions section. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Defines the de facto regime in Haiti (the held text spans a page break inside this item). Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Defines United States person. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Defines goods of Haitian origin. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

States that the measures are not intended to block private Haitian assets or to prohibit remittances to Haitian persons other than the regime. Later event: EO 12853 (signed 1993-06-30) Sec. 7 revokes sections 2(c) and 4 of EO 12779 to the extent inconsistent with EO 12853, effective immediately under its Sec. 8(a); EO 12853 Sec. 3 adds prohibitions on petroleum and arms and Sec. 4 limits the food exemption in section 2(c)(iii) for transactions involving the regime or identified persons, so the revocation reaches only that overlap. The clause continues until EO 12932. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation with the Secretary of State, to issue regulations under IEEPA, including on transportation by vessel or aircraft between the United States and Haiti, and directs agencies to cooperate. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Fixes the order's effective time as 11:59 p.m. Eastern standard time on November 5, 1991, and recites that Sec. 1 and 2(a) became effective at 12:23 p.m. on October 4, 1991 under EO 12775. An effective-date provision is spent when the stated time arrives, 1991-11-05.

States that the order confers no substantive or procedural right enforceable against the United States. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

Revokes EO 12775 to the extent inconsistent with this order, keeps delegations, rules and licenses under EO 12775 in force under this order until amended or terminated, and preserves liability for violations during the period a revoked provision was in effect, and directs transmittal to the Congress and publication. A conditional partial revocation of another order persists as long as the inconsistency, so it runs with this order. The held text does not show when, or whether, the Congress transmittal was made, so no earlier performance date is established. Ends with the order: EO 12932 (signed 1994-10-14; 59 FR 52403, Federal Register of October 18, 1994) revokes this order by number ("I hereby revoke Executive Order Nos. 12775, 12779, 12853, 12872, 12914," 12917, 12920, and 12922, and terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775) and provides "This order shall take effect at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on October" 16, 1994, so the end is 1994-10-16.

conflict_resolutions.FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT: The dossier flags that the sources read as both a whole and a partial ending for EO 12932. Resolution: EO 12932 revokes this order by number in a single sentence that names eight orders and also terminates the national emergency declared in EO 12775, so it is a whole ending. Earlier partial provisions held for some of these orders (revocations to the extent inconsistent in later Haiti orders) are recorded as later events of the clauses they touch; each is conditional on inconsistency and none is shown to extinguish a clause, so none is an end.

research_rationale:
EO 12779 of October 28, 1991 (Prohibiting Certain Transactions With Respect to Haiti), read in full in the held Federal Register text (56 FR 55975, Federal Register of October 30, 1991; machine-extracted text layer). Identity: number and subject agree with the census register row (1991-10-28); the held text layer's heading reads October 23, 1991 while its signature line reads October 28, 1991 (the heading digit looks like a scan misreading), and I use the register's and signature line's date. The order additionally blocks the Haitian Government's property, bars payments, imports and exports, defines terms, authorizes Treasury regulations, states its effective time, and revokes EO 12775 to the extent inconsistent. Inventory correction: the dossier inventory begins at Sec. 2 and omits Sec. 1 (the blocking command); I re-marked Sec. 1 on the held text and kept the dossier's spans for the rest, 15 clauses in all. EO 12932 revokes the order by number effective 12:01 a.m. EDT October 16, 1994. Own-terms end: Sec. 2(d) lapsed 30 days after the effective date. Later events: EO 12853 and EO 12917 revoke parts of Sec. 2(c) and Sec. 4 to the extent inconsistent. Searches: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts) were chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no scope warning. Machine hits for this order: current-law:usc 0, current-law:ecfr 0, later-events:ofr_catalog 14. The packet's by-number scan of held order texts (LOOKUPS) was read for this order; held texts citing this number include EO 12853, 12914, 12917, 12920, 12922 and 12932.

savings.reason: EO 12932 states that the termination of the national emergency does not affect any action taken or proceeding pending, any action or proceeding based on an act committed before its effective date, or any rights or duties that matured or penalties incurred before it. Those preserved effects, and any Treasury regulations or licenses issued under the order, are accrued consequences or separate administrative acts; they are not commands of this order. No held source shows an independent standing command of this order after 1994-10-16.
